explain.say: A lead-acid battery has lead plates in sulphuric acid. It is heavy and holds little energy for its weight, but it is cheap, tough and gives a huge burst of current, perfect for starting a car engine.

explain.say: Compare the energy stored in each kilogram: about 35 watt-hours for lead-acid, but around 160 to 250 for lithium-ion. That is why phones and electric cars use lithium-ion.
Lead-acid still wins on price and recycling, with nearly all old car batteries recycled in many countries. Lithium-ion needs more care, as damaged cells can overheat and catch fire.

faq.q: How does a lead-acid battery work?
faq.a: It has plates of lead and lead dioxide in sulphuric acid. As it discharges, both plates turn into lead sulphate and the acid gets weaker; charging reverses the reaction.
asks: What is inside a car battery?

faq.q: Why are lithium-ion batteries so light?
faq.a: Lithium is the lightest metal, so its ions carry charge with very little mass. Each lithium-ion cell also gives about 3.6 volts, compared with 2 volts for lead-acid, so fewer cells are needed.
asks: Why do lithium batteries hold more energy?

faq.q: Why do cars still use lead-acid batteries?
faq.a: A car starter battery must give hundreds of amps for a few seconds, work in freezing cold and cost little. Lead-acid does all that cheaply, even though it is heavy.
asks: Why not use lithium for car starter batteries?

faq.a: Lead-acid batteries are among the most recycled products in the world, with nearly all the lead reused. Lithium-ion recycling is growing to recover lithium, cobalt and nickel.

faq.q: Why can lithium-ion batteries catch fire?
faq.a: If a cell is damaged, overcharged or overheated, the separator can fail and the electrodes short-circuit, heating the flammable electrolyte. This can spread to nearby cells, called thermal runaway, so batteries have protection circuits.

facts: Gaston Planté invented the rechargeable lead-acid battery in 1859.
A lead-acid cell gives about 2 volts, so a 12 volt car battery contains six cells.
